newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Vranitzky wins agreement on Albania poll.
newsitem.headline: Vranitzky wins agreement on Albania poll.

text.p: European envoy Franz Vranitzky claimed a breakthrough on Friday in plans to hold early elections in Albania, saying the 10 main parties had signed a political contract to ensure the vote went ahead.
"This is a breakthrough which we have achieved today," Vranitzky told a news conference announcing the six-point contract.
"However I hasten to add that bringing it to reality is of course still a very important task by Albanian politicians, by the international community," he said.
Albanian President Sali Berisha hailed the contract as a real and important contribution.
"President Berisha expresses his determination to be committed and to contribute in the implementation of this agreement," a statement from his office said.

Vranitzky was on his fourth visit since widespread rioting over failed pyramid savings schemes broke out in February. A former Austrian chancellor, he is now acting as envoy of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe.

He said the impasse on the form of the election to be held by the end of June would be resolved by finding a balance between those who favoured a majority vote and those who favoured proportional representation.
A decision on a new election law would be taken by Monday, May 12.
Under the contract, the Salvation Committees, citizens' groups set up after the rioting to restore order in southern Albania, would be dissolved at least 46 days before the election.
Vranitzky was vague as to who would decide whether the groups had in fact been dissolved, saying that the dissolution of the committees "should and will be a joint effort."

Berisha's Democratic Party, which had been reluctant to sign the contract, maintains that the committees are the armed wing of their main rivals, the Socialists. The Socialists deny they are linked with the committees.

Tritan Shehu, the leader of the Democrats and a former foreign minister, pointed out as he left the signing that the committees would have to be disbanded a day before the president signed a decree proclaiming an election.

"When I said this is a guarantee, on the basis of the signatures of the 10 party leaders then it is mainly a guarantee not for me, it's a guarantee among others for President Berisha to sign the decree," Vranitzky said.
The contract says every effort should be made to ensure free movement and access for all parties during the campaign.
It agrees to limit those banned from running in the election to former members of the Communist Political Bureau, state security police collaborators and people convicted of crimes against humanity.
This would free Socialist leader Fatos Nano, a senior communist official and former prime minister, to stand.
The contract also invites the international community to nominate a co-ordinator of international standing to make a final report on the electoral process, which the signatories would not contest.
Vranitzky said this clause was to produce a single international verdict on the election and avoid the problems of May 1996 when several groups monitored the vote, producing different reports.
The democrats won 122 seats in the last election. Some international observers said the result was seriously flawed and the opposition Socialists pulled out of the ballot late on polling day.
Vranitzky left for Vienna after the news conference, which had been delayed while last-minute negotiations took place on the former contract.
"The character of the paper is a commitment, an obligation by the 10 parties that form the Albanian government to do a lot of things," Vranitzky said.
